_comment: Externalized answer bank for ATS driver scripts (ashby_apply_driver.mjs, greenhouse_apply_driver.mjs). Loaded at startup. Regex strings are passed to `new RegExp(str, 'i')`, so escape every backslash twice when porting JS literals (e.g. `\\s` in JSON == `\s` in JS).

essay_templates.match: tell us why.{0,30}good fit|why.{0,20}good fit|good fit for this position
essay_templates.answer_template: I am a strong fit for {{COMPANY_PRETTY}} because {{WHY_ROLE}}. My academic background in {{MAJOR}} at {{SCHOOL}}, combined with my project and work experience, has trained me to learn quickly, communicate clearly, and turn ambiguous tasks into useful output. I would bring ownership, careful execution, and curiosity to the internship from day one.

One project I am proud of is {{FAVORITE_PROJECT}}. What made it meaningful was owning the full loop: understanding the problem, building or organizing a first version, getting feedback, and improving it instead of stopping at an idea. That experience is also why I am interested in internships where I can contribute real work and keep learning from practical constraints.

I have not had a dedicated GIS title unless noted in my resume, but I am comfortable working with structured data, research workflows, source tracking, and careful data quality checks. If the role uses a GIS stack I have not used before, I would be honest about that and ramp quickly through documentation, examples, and feedback from the team.

essay_templates.match: what would make joining chai a win.?win
essay_templates.answer_template: A win for {{COMPANY_PRETTY}} would be getting an intern who learns fast, communicates clearly, and can take a loosely defined problem through research, execution, and iteration. A win for me would be learning from a strong team while contributing real work that makes the team faster or more informed.

A bet I have is that students and early-career builders can create much more leverage when they combine strong judgment with modern AI and automation tools. The important part is not using tools as shortcuts; it is using them to test ideas faster, document assumptions, and make better decisions with evidence.

essay_templates.match: highlight of your career|something you built.*meaningful|something you accomplished
essay_templates.answer_template: A highlight so far is {{FAVORITE_PROJECT}}. It mattered because it required more than completing a task; I had to make decisions, learn what was not working, and improve the result based on feedback. That experience shaped how I work: start with a clear goal, ship a real version, listen carefully, and iterate.

One topic I have been following is how AI changes early-career work: not just by generating drafts, but by helping people research, prototype, analyze, and iterate faster. I am especially interested in where human judgment still matters most: choosing the right problem, checking quality, communicating clearly, and understanding users or customers.

I am interested in {{COMPANY_PRETTY}} because {{WHY_COMPANY}}. The role also fits my current direction: {{WHY_ROLE}}. I am looking for an internship where I can contribute useful work, learn from a strong team, and build judgment through real execution rather than only classroom theory.

A project I would highlight is {{FAVORITE_PROJECT}}. It reflects the way I like to work: start from a real problem, build or organize a concrete solution, learn from feedback, and improve the result. More detail is available here if useful: {{PORTFOLIO}}.

I use AI tools to speed up research, drafting, analysis, and iteration, while still checking the work carefully. The best use case for me is not outsourcing judgment; it is getting to a first version faster, testing assumptions, and improving quality through review. I am especially interested in practical workflows where AI helps a team move faster without losing accuracy.

essay_templates.match: which areas of marketing are you most interested
essay_templates.answer_template: Demand generation/lead generation, content marketing, and analytics/reporting. I like the part of marketing where messaging, audience insight, channel experiments, and funnel metrics meet, because you can quickly see whether the work is creating qualified pipeline.

Good marketing makes the right customer understand the problem, trust the solution, and take the next useful step. I know it is working when it improves measurable behavior: qualified traffic, conversion between funnel stages, CAC/payback, retention, or sales feedback quality.

I would first want to understand the ICP, the funnel model, current goals, what channels are already working, what data the team trusts, and where handoffs with sales or client teams break down. Then I would look for small experiments I can help ship quickly.

essay_templates.match: if yes, please briefly describe.*email marketing|context in which you used it
essay_templates.answer_template: I have used email in student, project, or work contexts to communicate with specific audiences, draft clear messages, and track whether the message led to the intended next step. My main takeaway is that email works best when it is specific to the audience, concise, and tied to a clear action.

essay_templates.match: what experience.*demand generation internship|what experience.*help you succeed
essay_templates.answer_template: My strongest relevant experience is combining research, communication, and execution. Through coursework, projects, and prior experience, I have practiced turning an audience or business problem into a hypothesis, a message, a channel or workflow, and a simple metric to learn from.
My earliest listed start date is {{EARLIEST_START_DATE}}. I can typically discuss internship availability around my academic calendar, and I can provide exact timing if the recruiting team needs it.

Any gaps reflect school terms, independent projects, and student commitments rather than a break from professional interest or availability.

essay_templates.match: (what kind of work environment|work environment are you looking for|preferred work environment)
essay_templates.answer_template: I do my best work in an environment with clear goals, direct feedback, and room to take ownership. I like teams that move quickly but communicate well, where interns can contribute practical work, ask thoughtful questions, and learn from people who care about quality.

essay_templates.match: (years? of experience.{0,40}relevant|total years? of experience|experience you have that are relevant)
essay_templates.answer_template: My relevant experience comes from the projects, coursework, and roles listed in my resume, especially {{LATEST_TITLE}} at {{LATEST_COMPANY}}. I am still early-career, so I would describe my experience in terms of concrete resume-backed work rather than claiming a fixed number of years unless a recruiter needs a specific format.

One trend I am excited about is the shrinking distance between identifying a problem and testing a real solution. AI and automation make it easier for small teams and students to prototype, analyze, and iterate quickly. That makes judgment, communication, and customer understanding even more important, because speed only matters when you are working on the right problem.

One of my strengths is {{BIGGEST_STRENGTH}}. I work well when there is a clear goal but some ambiguity in how to reach it, because I am comfortable asking good questions, making a first plan, and improving through feedback.

A growth area for me is {{BIGGEST_WEAKNESS}}. I am working on it by asking for feedback earlier, writing down decisions more clearly, and making sure my work is easy for teammates or managers to understand and build on.
